description.narrative:
This is a one-year project with Major Donor funding, which is in addition to the ongoing annual grant from CAFOD to CDC for “Institutional and Supporting Activities” (ETM114). It will provide for certain material inputs for income-generation activities, and the conduct of specified activities designed to strengthen local supply chains and increase market opportunities in and around Baucau.
CDC has as their overall objective the promotion of local initiatives towards sustainable economic development with a focus on the District of Baucau. This work is centred on support to women’s food processing groups and the farmers who supply them. CDC believes that only by increasing income generation opportunities can Timor enjoy sustained economic growth and peace. Their programme has developed strategically and organically as they have been responding to the needs of small local groups over the years, effectively giving them a helping hand following their own initiative to overcome poverty. The support they give to these groups includes particular skills training and the setting up of links between farmers, producers and processors of agricultural goods, such as fruits, tomatoes, small fish and vegetables. Through this a market is guaranteed for small local farmers, and income is generated for the processing groups, and in particular women, who otherwise face significant challenges in accessing the job market.
Through this additional one-year project, CDC will be able to enhance its support to three of the women's processing groups, and strengthen the local supply chain links and marketing opportunities. Specifically it will fund: 1) the construction of new kitchens for three women's food processing groups; 2) the conduct of field research, mapping, and mobilisation of local farmers; 3) the provision of seeds and tools to local farmers, and; 4) the establishment of a co-operatively managed sales outlet in Baucau.
